text: This is one of the few adventure/sandbox games that I found frustrating to play. With lack of proper tutorial or instruction, this game is pretty hard to play by jumping right into it. I did end up exiting, and didn't go back. I will probably find my way back to this game in the future, kicking and screaming. I'm not going to recommend this game, for several reasons: 1. This game is tough to understand. That's a subjective statement, but I will stand by it; it plays like a game trying to be more than it actually is. Why complicate the game with things that it really doesn't need? And why push it all on a new player at once? The menus are atrocious and simply not conducive to someone trying to play the game for the first time. 2. This game will likely never be fixed or revamped. The latest developer news included this passage: "Piracy is buggy and the internal code is messy, it'd take a whole new code base to FIX it, and. While we can never remake it, look out for Q1 2016, but that's a different piece of news for a different moment [...]". I'm not a developer, and don't claim to know what they're doing, but it sounds like they're dumping Pixel Piracy for a new game they're developing: Pixel Privateers. I bought this game while it was in Early Access, hoping it would amount to something. It didn't, and I believe it's just another excuse to point and scream at the Early Access system, ignoring the fact that this game doesn't feel planned at all, and just a collection of random ideas thrown into a game by three people. Is this game worth it, to the objective buyer? I would say no. You're better off saving your money, and scoping out their new game. Now that they've had what I will deem a flop, they have no excuses, barring acts of god, to drop the ball again. And with their new game being in the same style, with the same concept (Pirates/Sea Adventure), the expectations are even higher.

text: Hello possible commanders, so I shall "judge" this game. Judging is a personal thing, so here are my impressions: We all hailed supreme commander. So very different units, so many commander upgrades. With expansions, some things became quite imbalanced if you rushed them. Scale and performance had always been an issue (I had no 1000 $ for a top notch gaming machine). Planetary Annihilation has all those units, but makes them available for all. Now it is up to you to crush your enemy with titans, flood him with mechs, bomb him to the ground, nuke him to death, crush him under the tires and chains of yourt tanks or eradicate the planet he dwells on (preferably you have a transport or "warpgate" if you also happen to dwell on that planet) with an asteroid, a moon, or a planet-killer gun. It also has: strategic flexibility a factor of randomness (galactic war) balance: if the enemy has warships, you have a simple defense gun that mows the orbit free  Because I am a beta backer, I have no idea how many skins are for free, but they are mostly cosmetic. The available basic commanders have the same armament for free. Then comes planetary annihilation. I was one of the beta buyers/testers. There were good days, there were sad days. There were bugs. Unfinished units. Planetary travel problems (you had no idea how to do it)... and so on. Considering bugs (and with the AI): They fixed them, made it a funny yet sometimes hard game when the AI came killing you wit a super army. (Only one time an enemy subcommander marched directly onto my warships. The idea was good - they had no underwater defense. Problem - massive firepower and single target enemy. So not a real bug but you might think it was one.) Planetary Annihilation: Titans has not disappointed me. Get it for the special offer price, it is totally worth it. If you like the genre and loved supreme commander - get it as well. Some thoughts: Planetary scale - no other game has it. Warp in reinforcements? Why not fly them from another planet. Or deliver them via planet (not recommended) Nuclear missile - meh. Why not crush the enemy with an asteroid? Or two? We still have those tough 2d maps, her you get a whole solar system. As of yet, I have to discover any AI unfairness. Concerning dlc, i have seen no such thing, just got some free commander skins. Or models. Scouts are useful. Radar is useful. If you use them, it is very easy to find your enemy. On larger planets tough, it takes some time to find the opposition - because the radar has limited range. Also, I have yet to play on a world that was covered to more than 40% with water. As I play the game, i will update the review. (UPDATE 1) Great game. Really funny moments, where i died in the campaign, yes, you can call it that, because I pressed the planetary ignition button. Stupid tough, because my escape ship was shot down and the teleport was on the target planet. Compared to many other games, the "galactic war" is a campaign. I call it that, read the information on each planet and enemy commander, and decide for yourself. (UPDATE 2) Played some intergalactic Maps with aquatic planets. Works awesomely smooth. Water land transition is neatless and all working just fine. Teleporters are really useful and fun - even on a single planet when you want to install a beachhead infront of your enemies base because a mountan blocks his artillery. Orbital teleport titans are also really fantastic - invasion on a new level. You should shield the more valuable assault titan with "replaceable" interstallar ships tough - 3 basic space defense buildings wreck your priceless armada in a second. Also, for the first time, used the planetkiller (metal planet with 5 catalyst units) on a moving planetary object. Really and imply epic. YOu even can deploy or move units off that rock or out of its orbit in mere seconds before the impact.

You can build nothing but builders and defenses, then nuke the world into submission (like the terran's from StarCraft). You can spam cheap units early on and try to rush them (Zerg).
